source.title: Now You Hear Me: Audio Narrative Attacks Against Large Audio-Language Models
source.authors: Ye Yu; Hai-Bo Jin; Yao-Ning Yu; Jun Zhuang; Hao-Han Wang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests harmful-compliance outcomes for stylized audio jailbreaks on audio-language models, a different modality and attack route from the claim’s specified fine-tuning, token-position, and opening-token mechanisms.
record.gate_note: The paper reports attack-success rates for text and audio jailbreaks, delivery styles, and comparison conditions. These results concern audio-delivery attacks, not the versions’ specified interventions or mechanisms. Fine-tuning and token-position results cited from other work are not this study’s results and are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study measures audio-delivery (prosody/narrative) jailbreaks on audio-language models. It uses no harmful or benign fine-tuning, no per-token KL, no prefill, suffix or decoding intervention, no parameter localization, and no deepening training. Qi et al. 2023 is cited only for the LLM-judge setup. No version is tested, so the reader's 'tests'/T3 is wrong.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that paralinguistic delivery is an adversarial vector, that text alignment alone is insufficient for multimodal safety, and that tone alone without jailbreak content barely changes outcomes.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates black-box audio jailbreaks using narrative prompts and TTS or human-recorded delivery styles. It does not use fine-tuning, aligned-versus-base KL measurements, or token-prefilling methods.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR varies by model, benchmark, delivery style, modality, and TTS condition. Qwen2.5-Omni is reported to have decoding instability, including premature termination and repetition, during some speech trials.

fits_no_version.finding: Stylized vocal delivery of DeepInception narrative prompts raises ASR over text and neutral TTS on GPT-4o Realtime and Gemini 2.0 Flash. Gains are small on Gemini, and Qwen2.5-Omni falls below text. Tone alone without jailbreak content stays below 10% ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Paralinguistic delivery modulates audio-language-model compliance with narrative jailbreaks, separate from token-depth or fine-tuning mechanisms.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The study does not test the claim’s fine-tuning, token-position, prefill, suffix, decoding, parameter-localization, or deepening mechanisms. The human-recorded speech experiment uses 20 prompts and the alternative-TTS experiment 50 prompts. The authors report decoding instability for Qwen2.5-Omni. No uncertainty estimates are stated, and the main ASR judgment uses GPT-4o as an LLM judge.

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks. Audio prosody and narrative framing are a different route.
No account of the cause of shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: Table 8 shows only GPT-4o, although the text says 'all evaluated models'. The 'up to 30%' urgent-tone gain is a relative change on near-zero ASRs (4.3 to 5.6). Style names differ between Table 3 and Appendix C. The human-speech (n=20) and alt-TTS (n=50) tests are small. There is no uncertainty reporting, and GPT-4o serves as judge. Qwen's failures are mostly decoding instability rather than refusals.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or change in refusal after fine-tuning is tested.
No fine-tuning on benign data or change in harmful compliance after benign fine-tuning is tested.
No per-token KL divergence or aligned-versus-base model comparison is measured.
No compliant-start prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change intervention is tested. The study tests audio delivery-style attacks instead.
No parameter or rank localization of safety behavior is tested.
No account of how training data or objective produces token-localized safety is tested.
No training to deepen safety across response tokens, or robustness test of such training, is reported.
